messages:
taylor_pm: quick follow-up from today's all-hands: two asks — (1) confirm release cadence for the next quarter, and (2) what's the explicit oncall behavior during canary windows? also, what minimum quality bar do we require before kicking off a canary?

mina_eng: TL;DR: monthly feature releases (aim first week of month) + ad-hoc patch lane. feature-freeze = 10 days before ship week.

elaine_cto: canaries are default for non-explosive infra and model changes. typical canary window 12-48h. we use a rolling promotion: 5% -> 20% -> 50% as long as health checks are green.

mina_eng: gates we use: P95 latency <= 1.2x baseline, error-rate delta < 0.1% absolute, infra errors < threshold, and no new user-facing regressions on CI smoke. for inference changes also require model-eval set drift < 1% on key prompts.

release-helper-bot: Release runbook updated: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/releases (freeze checklist, canary dashboard link, PR template) :link:

sre_lead: oncall expectations: canary_owner listed in PR is primary responder for the window and must post a kickoff in #eng-oncall. we prefer pairing oncall for first 2 hours of a canary for risky changes. if a route has SLA tags (tier=dedicated), SRE must be cc'd before any promotion beyond 20%.

mina_eng: if flaky tests appear after canary starts: suspend promotion, mark the test as flaky in CI, open a P1 ticket if signals are noisy, and aim for triage within 4h. rollback runway: if metrics oscillate > guardrail for more than 30m, roll back.

docs-team: engineers keep asking for a concrete PR body snippet. dropping one below to paste into rollout PRs.

```
canary_owner: @username
canary_start_utc: 2026-09-03 15:00 UTC
traffic_plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 36h
health_gates: p95_latency, error_rate, smoke_regressions, model_eval_delta
rollback_runway: metrics stable window < 30m => rollback
sla_routes: [customer/dedicated/*]
canary_dashboard: <dashboard URL>
```

elaine_cto: note on SLAs: Legal/Ops still finalizing the contract text, but engineering target = avoid >10% P99 regression on SLA-monitored routes post-deploy. treat SLA-tagged routes as high-sensitivity during canary.

taylor_pm: great, i'll summarize and push to the all-hands notes + link runbook. planning a 15min office hour tomorrow 9am PT for any teams with upcoming rollouts.

sre_lead: action items: update PR template, add canary pairing recommendation to runbook, publish canary dashboard link in runbook.

release-helper-bot: Reminder: next oncall rotation begins 1950040000.

taylor_pm: thanks everyone — closing thread after office hour doc is posted. :thumbsup:
